scope: Manual source/initialization argument for meaningful callback state; not a formal proof or board qualification.
findings: watch() registers the callback before the port metadata (including pp->ctx and pp->handle) is assigned. A registration handoff may store opaque port/signal/callback/function identities, but must defer reading that port metadata until initialization completes.

Before invoking each live value callback, run_vpi_callbacks() refreshes its value via get_value(). output_cb() copies the vector words into pp->new and returns without yielding. The temporary value union is not surviving bridge state at the subsequent synchronization pause.

The known watch caller initializes callback user_data, object, function, vector format and suppressed time. The observer validates those relationships and actual signal-list membership, without reading unused index or suppressed time/value storage.

Cancellation clears cb_rtn immediately; a subsequent signal change removes the callback from its list and invokes its destructor. The registry erases its entry at destruction. Controls cover head and non-head removal.
next: Integrate explicit watch-registration handoff with the initialized-port observer. Check every output/inout port has one registered callback with the original lifetime ID; exercise restored faults against the complete bounded board with the matched original-runtime baseline.
